article.title: Common mistake: 'I am agree' vs 'I agree'
article.description: Wrong: 'I am agree with you.' Right: 'I agree with you.' Teaching point: 'agree' is already a verb in English, unlike some languages where the equivalent is an adjective/state requiring 'to be'. No 'am/is/are' needed before 'agree'.
article.content: Wrong: 'I am agree with you.' Right: 'I agree with you.' Teaching point: 'agree' is already a verb in English, unlike some languages where the equivalent is an adjective/state requiring 'to be'. No 'am/is/are' needed before 'agree'.

generated.caption:
Ever said "I am agree" and felt a tiny bit unsure? 🤔 It's a common mistake!

In English, 'agree' is already a verb, so you don't need 'am/is/are' before it. Think of it like this: "I agree with you." Easy to remember, right? 😊

Save this quick tip & share it with a friend! Follow @EnglishVault for daily lessons. #EnglishTips
generated.script: Aapne bhi kabhi 'I am agree' bola hai kya? Sunne mein theek lagta hai, par ye galat hai! Basically, 'agree' jo hai na, woh already ek verb hai. Matlab, isko kisi 'am', 'is', 'are' ki zaroorat nahi hai. Jaise hum 'I am go' nahi bolte, 'I go' bolte hain. Waise hi, 'I am agree' nahi, 'I agree'. For example, 'I agree with you'. Toh next time se, remember, 'I am agree' nahi, sirf 'I agree'. Simple! Comment karke batao aapne ye mistake ki thi ya nahi, aur follow karo The English Vault ko!

slides.body: Many English learners often mistakenly say 'I am agree,' but this is a common grammatical error. In English, 'agree' is already a complete verb, meaning 'to have the same opinion.' Therefore, you do not need to add a form of 'to be' (like 'am,' 'is,' or 'are') before it, unlike in some other languages where an equivalent might be an adjective requiring 'to be.' The correct way to express your assent is simply 'I agree.' For example, instead of saying, 'I am agree with you,' you should always say, 'I agree with you.'
